Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   - **Octopus routing & queue clearing**: User had 73 stuck Octopus-authored issues (#13994–#14071) that weren't flowing through the WR pipeline. Wanted them translated and routed to openrouter-coder.
   - **Fix recurring agent output problems**: Across ~40 PRs, agents were producing junk WRs with scaffolding leak, raw `{STARS}` tokens, wrong template usage, body-in-table-cell, and "documents the fix but doesn't apply it" patterns.
   - **Implement REVVEL/UPREV system**: User shared MASTER.md + 7 zip files from a parallel session containing: MASTER.md system-of-record, WR templates (BASIC/FULL), generate-wr.sh, wr-lint.mjs, fix-wr-gate.mjs, CI workflows. Asked to "implement all this".
   - **Persona renames for memorability**: User couldn't remember which of oAudrey/Professor/MindMappr/RadioChaser did what. Wanted role-descriptive names. I proposed Triager/Citer/Spotter/Standby. User said "i like your names" and asked "but the new names can use @?" — I clarified `/` only, not `@`.
   - **Tier 2/Tier 3 fixes**: Address WR generator bugs (Tier 2) and "documents but doesn't fix" pattern (Tier 3) from Octopus dump triage.

   Security/critical constraints (verbatim):
   - "GitHub treats `@name` as a mention of the real user account with that username and emails them — so the old `@professor` syntax pinged a stranger who owns the `@professor` handle on every comment. The slash form never notifies anyone." — Persona triggers MUST use `/` not `@`.
   - "I dont want quadrails. It screws them up... they are not an llm and cannot do quadrails effectively" — Don't add safety/ethics prose to agent prompts.
   - "nothing should ever be dropped just commented out" — Comment-don't-delete convention.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - REVVEL/UPREV system: MASTER.md as system-of-record, UPREV method (one iteration, max over minimum, form-driven not label-driven)
   - WR generator pipeline: TITLE_TO_WR_EXPANSION → research mandate → artifact generator → work_request.yml schema → Jules normalize → execute → wr-lint
   - Persona system: PERSONA_REGISTRY with handles + aliases, slash-trigger (`/name`) to avoid notifying real GitHub users
   - Five recurring WR failure classes: scaffolding leak, wrong template, raw tokens, false-checked checklist, body-in-table-cell
   - Sixth pattern (highest severity): "documents fix but doesn't apply it"
   - GitHub Actions: `fetch-depth: 0` requirement, event-payload SHAs for determinism, GITHUB_TOKEN can't trigger another workflow
   - Linter false-positive avoidance: tracking fenced code blocks via `inFence[]` array

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - **PR #14219 (Tier 1 — MERGED)**: Fixed `scripts/audit-third-party-actions.sh` (case-insensitive contains, BSD `date -j -f` fallback, calendar-accurate threshold math `(N * 3044 + 50) / 100`) and `.github/workflows/third-party-action-audit.yml` (SHA-pinned actions, closed shell injection vector via `REPORT_FILE` env var).
   - **PR #14227 (REVVEL/UPREV system)**: Landed 9 files: MASTER.md, workflows/TITLE_TO_WR_EXPANSION.md, wr/WR_TEMPLATE_BASIC.md, wr/WR_TEMPLATE_FULL.md, wr/scripts/generate-wr.sh, wr/scripts/wr-lint.mjs, wr/scripts/fix-wr-gate.mjs, .github/workflows/wr-lint.yml, .github/workflows/fix-wr-gate.yml. Replaced existing buggy templates that were source of scaffolding leak.
   - **PR #14227 follow-up commits**: 
     - VADE fix (commit ef6f214): added `fetch-depth: 0` to wr-lint.yml
     - Copilot+Devin+VADE fixes (commit cdb7e48): 12 fixes including critical HTML-comment-stripping in generate-wr.sh:
       ```bash
       out="$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk '
         BEGIN { stripping=1 }
         stripping && /^<!--.*-->[[:space:]]*$/ { next }
         stripping && /^[[:space:]]*$/           { next }
         { stripping=0; print }
       ')"
       ```
     - Fixed ERE `\b` bug:
       ```bash
       if echo "$TITLE" | grep -qwiE '(fix|bug|typo|lint|refactor|chore|docs?|remove|pin|normalize|standardize|unreachable|duplicate)'; then
       ```
     - Added `inFence[]` tracking to wr-lint.mjs:
       ```javascript
       const inFence = new Array(lines.length).fill(false);
       let fenced = false;
       lines.forEach((l, i) => {
         if (/^```/.test(l.trim())) fenced = !fenced;
         inFence[i] = fenced;
       });
       ```
     - jq_get returns "N/A" instead of empty:
       ```bash
       jq_get() {
         local v
         v="$(echo "$META" | (command -v jq >/dev/null && jq -r ".$1 // \"\"" || echo ""))"
         [[ -z "$v" ]] && echo "N/A" || echo "$v"
       }
       ```
   - **Branch claude/persona-role-rename (CURRENT — pushed, no PR opened yet)**: 
     - `scripts/openrouter-personas.js`: Added `aliases: ["triager", "triage"]` to oaudrey, `aliases: ["citer", "sourcer"]` to professor, `aliases: ["spotter"]` to mindmappr, `aliases: ["dispatcher", "router"]` to openrouter. Extended `getPersona()`:
       ```javascript
       if (PERSONA_REGISTRY[key]) return PERSONA_REGISTRY[key];
       for (const p of Object.values(PERSONA_REGISTRY)) {
         if ((p.aliases || []).map((a) => a.toLowerCase()).includes(key)) return p;
       }
       ```
     - `scripts/persona-comment-runner.js`: Extended `parsePersonaCommand` to collect canonical + aliases into `triggerToHandle` map, then maps back to canonical handle.
     - `.github/workflows/ready-for-review.yml`: Roster table now shows `**oAudrey · Triager**`, `**The Professor · Citer**`, `**MindMappr · Spotter**`, `**RadioChaser · Standby**` with both trigger forms.

4. Errors and fixes:
   - **Critical Devin finding**: HTML comments before H1 in WR_TEMPLATE_FULL.md caused generator to always fail its own lint gate (H1 at line 3, not 1). Fixed with awk strip.
   - **Copilot `\b` ERE bug**: ERE doesn't support `\b` word boundaries — auto-classification never matched. Fixed with `grep -wiE` and `\<...\>` POSIX boundaries.
   - **Empty meta contract violation**: subst() wrote empty strings, violating "fill or N/A" contract. Fixed to return "N/A".
   - **wr-lint false positives in fenced code**: 5 rules (H1, raw brackets, tokens, bracket placeholders, table-cell) all fired inside ```yaml blocks. Fixed with `inFence` skip.
   - **VADE missing fetch-depth**: wr-lint.yml shallow clone caused diff fallback to lint ALL existing wr/issues files. Fixed with `fetch-depth: 0`.
   - **Workflow base ref non-determinism**: switched both workflows from `origin/${BASE}` to event-payload `base.sha`/`head.sha`.
   - **User feedback "guardrails screw agents up"**: User explicitly rejected prose-style ethical guardrails because their non-LLM review agents can't process them effectively.
   - **User feedback "@ pings real users"**: When asked if new aliases support `@triager` form, I clarified NO — must use `/` only.

Roo Code's "team" is its mode system — Architect, Code, Debug, Ask, Orchestrator — each a specialized sub-agent that can hand work off to the others. Right now in our roster Roo just gets pinged for the testing checklist section, which throws away ~90% of what it can do.

Best use given the free-on-GitHub window: route Coder/Fixer work through Roo's Orchestrator mode (it picks Architect → Code → Debug automatically) instead of openrouter-coder for the fix lane — Roo's multi-step agent loop is meaningfully better at "diagnose then patch" than a single OpenRouter call. The tradeoff is exactly what you flagged: they're leaving the market, so anything we wire to Roo needs a fallback (route through OpenRouter Coder if Roo unavailable) so we're not stranded when it goes away.

## 🤖 assistant

Roo wired into PR #14234. Summary:

- **Workflow renamed** to `Coder (Roo primary → OpenRouter fallback)`
- **Roo step**: runs only when `ROO_API_KEY` secret is set; uses Orchestrator mode (Architect → Code → Debug loop) by default; `continue-on-error: true` so any Roo outage soft-fails into OpenRouter
- **OpenRouter step**: now gated on `steps.roo.outcome != 'success' || steps.roo.outputs.files_written == '0'` — true fallback, no double-execution
- **Override hatch**: `ROO_RUN_COMMAND` repo variable lets you point at whatever Roo surface you actually have (cloud API curl, different CLI, etc.) without editing the workflow
- **VADE finding fixed**: tests updated from 4 → 5 personas (27/27 passing)

To activate Roo: set the `ROO_API_KEY` secret on the repo. Until then OpenRouter remains the only coder lane — zero behavior change.

## 🧑 user

this is it right? When we started Roo Code in late 2024 by forking Cline and adding what's now widely known as dangerously-skip-permissions, agentic coding was rough and experimental. But Roo Code took off fast: 3 million installs, a passionate community, real innovation that pushed the space forward. It was the beginning of a new way of working in the IDE.

Article content
Where it all started
But by Fall 2025, we were seeing another big shift in how we worked internally. We were running Roo Code in cloud containers to parallelize work and keep up with hundreds of community PRs and issues. It worked headlessly with full auto-approve enabled, opened fixes, ran the actual app, and verified its own work before asking anyone to look. It quickly became the default way for us to work.

Prompt in → high-quality PR out.

If the agent can create a good PR from a single prompt, the interaction model changes completely: you let go of the IDE and focus on driving things end-to-end. The agent doesn't just help engineers - it wipes entire types of work off their plate and delivers something nobody has to clean up.

Meanwhile, tons of new harnesses arrived. Models improved, interfaces converged, first-party tools became discount token ATMs, and forks redistributed our work as fast as we shipped it. It became clear: we were winning at something that we didn't think mattered anymore.

So we made the call. Not because Roo Code failed, but because the world it served would cease to exist. We're letting it go because we're already all-in on what comes next.

We call our cloud agent Roomote. It rocks. It lives in Slack with the rest of your team, integrates into all of your tools (Linear, Github, Sentry, etc), and runs whichever frontier model fits the job. It verifies its own work with screenshots and a full local environment, so PMs, support, ops, marketers, and founders also get real PRs done end-to-end. It's not a tool, but a real teammate.

Article content
Talking to Roomote all day every day
In practice: we’re archiving the Roo Code repo, refunding any unused balances, and making the last extension release on May 15th. To our community, we thank you deeply. If you still need an extension, Cline has incorporated many of the Roo Code features and will welcome you with open arms. But we invite you to come figure out with us: what does a software team look like when the agents aren't tools, but teammates?

Join the Roomote waitlist at https://roomote.dev. We're letting people in daily.

1	#!/usr/bin/env node
2	// fix-wr-gate.mjs — closes the "documents the fix but doesn't apply it" hole.
3	// A fix-class WR PR must EITHER touch a real (non-wr/) file, OR be explicitly labeled tracking-only.
4	// Catches PRs #14186/#14185/#14177/#14138/#14116/#14066 etc. pattern.
5	//
6	// Usage: node fix-wr-gate.mjs --changed <file-list-newline-or-comma> [--labels <csv>] [--title "<pr title>"]
7	//   exit 0 = pass, 1 = gate violation.
8	//
9	// "Real fix" = any changed file NOT under wr/ and NOT a pure docs/tracking artifact.
10	// Tracking-only escape hatch = PR has a label in TRACKING_LABELS or title starts with a TRACKING_PREFIX.
11	
12	const args = process.argv.slice(2);
13	const get = (n) => { const i = args.indexOf(`--${n}`); return i >= 0 ? args[i + 1] : ""; };
14	
15	const changedRaw = get("changed");
16	const labels = get("labels").split(",").map((s) => s.trim().toLowerCase()).filter(Boolean);
17	const title = get("title") || "";
18	
19	const TRACKING_LABELS = ["tracking-only", "wr-docs", "wr-tracking", "meta-tracking", "docs-only"];
20	const TRACKING_PREFIXES = [/^\[wr-docs\]/i, /^\[wr-tracking\]/i, /^track\b/i, /^\[track\]/i];
21	
22	// Title signals this PR claims to FIX something (not just track it).
23	const FIX_SIGNAL = /\b(fix|resolve|repair|correct|patch|remove|add (missing|the)|implement)\b/i;
24	
25	const changed = changedRaw.split(/[\n,]/).map((s) => s.trim()).filter(Boolean);
26	
27	function isRealFix(path) {
28	  if (path.startsWith("wr/")) return false;                 // WR tracking docs don't count
29	  if (/^docs\/.*\.md$/i.test(path)) return true;            // a docs FIX (e.g. broken link) IS the fix
30	  return true;                                              // any code/config/workflow file counts
31	}
32	
33	const realFixFiles = changed.filter(isRealFix);
34	const wrOnly = changed.length > 0 && realFixFiles.length === 0;
35	const claimsFix = FIX_SIGNAL.test(title);
36	const isTrackingOnly =
37	  labels.some((l) => TRACKING_LABELS.includes(l)) ||
38	  TRACKING_PREFIXES.some((re) => re.test(title.trim()));
39	
40	const issues = [];
41	
42	if (claimsFix && wrOnly && !isTrackingOnly) {
43	  issues.push(
44	    `PR title claims a fix ("${title.trim()}") but the diff only touches wr/ tracking files ` +
45	    `(${changed.join(", ")}). Either include the actual fix (a non-wr/ file), OR label the PR ` +
46	    `one of [${TRACKING_LABELS.join(", ")}] / prefix the title "[WR-DOCS]" to mark it tracking-only.`
47	  );
48	}
49	
50	// Secondary: a fix WR that is tracking-only should SAY so, to avoid a future reviewer thinking it's resolved.
51	if (claimsFix && wrOnly && isTrackingOnly) {

53	}

## 🤖 assistant

The failure is a GitHub API rate-limit exhaustion on the installation token (request ID `1018:3A6700:...`), not a defect in the PR. The workflow couldn't post the freshness comment because GitHub throttled it. Transient — re-runs naturally on the next push/sync. No code action needed; if it stays red after the rate window resets, a manual re-run on that job will clear it.

### 🧠 thinking

> 

## 🤖 assistant

Nothing to pay — and you can't buy your way out of this one. The throttled token is the **installation `GITHUB_TOKEN`** that GitHub Actions hands every workflow run; its limit is 1,000 API requests/hour per repository and it's not on a plan. GitHub Free/Pro/Team all share the same ceiling. Enterprise raises it but isn't worth it for this.

The real cause is the AI-reviewer fleet hammering the API on every PR event:
- ~12 bots each do `listComments` + `createComment` + `updateComment`
- Multiple webhook triggers per push (open, sync, edit, label, comment) replay the same calls
- No `concurrency: cancel-in-progress` on most of them, so concurrent pushes pile up

Cheap fixes that actually work (in order of impact):
1. **Add `concurrency: cancel-in-progress`** to docs-freshness, ready-for-review, and the AI-reviewer workflows — kills the pileup
2. **Switch the noisier comment-posters from `GITHUB_TOKEN` to a PAT** (your user PAT gets 5,000/hr) — instant 5× headroom
3. **Cache `listComments` results** within a single run — most of these scripts call it 3-4 times

Want me to do (1) across the worst-offender workflows on a separate PR? That alone usually clears the throttling without any token changes.

## Security-class findings

**BLOCKER · `octopus-cli.yml:49` and `:66`** — Duplicate `invoke:` job key. YAML duplicate-key resolution silently drops the first job's `steps:`, so the parsed `invoke` job has **no steps at all** (verified). The workflow does literally nothing on `pull_request_target`. Additionally lines 60-65 (`if [ -z … ]`) are missing the closing `fi`, and lines 75-77 place YAML comments inside an `if:` expression. *Fix:* rename the second `invoke:` to `review:`, close the `fi`, move the security-rationale comment above `steps:`.

**BLOCKER · `jules-pr-reviewer.yml:75-76`** — Malformed YAML: orphaned `state: 'failure'` / `description:` keys floating at file root after the `script:` block ends. The whole file fails `yaml.safe_load` (verified). GitHub Actions will refuse to register this workflow. *Fix:* delete the orphaned lines, or move them inside the appropriate `createCommitStatus` payload.

**HIGH · `priority-router.yml:3-11`** — `pull_request_target` fires on `edited`, `labeled`, `unlabeled` from forks. The fork guard at line 318-322 only fires inside one branch of the script; the surrounding job has no top-level `if: head.repo.full_name == github.repository`, and earlier steps (line 47-52) already pass `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and `ADMIN_GITHUB_TOKEN` into the runner before the fork check. *Fix:* add `if: github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository || github.event_name != 'pull_request_target'` at the job level.

**HIGH · `openrouter-triage.yml:7-11`** — `pull_request_target` with no `head.repo.full_name` guard anywhere. Job at line 23 only filters by event name. Fork PRs can trigger the OpenRouter triage with `secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY` exposed in env (line 70/80). *Fix:* gate the `route-new` job with the standard fork-repo equality check.

**HIGH · `openrouter-assignee.yml:21,48`** — Same pattern: `pull_request_target` with no head-repo guard before label writes use `ADMIN_GITHUB_TOKEN` (line 125). Forks can spin this up hourly via the cron sweep too. *Fix:* add head-repo guard to `route-new`.

**HIGH · `duplicate-detector.yml:6, 22`** — `pull_request_target` with no fork-repo guard while using `ADMIN_GITHUB_TOKEN`. Issue search APIs (lines 39-50 in the script) run on attacker-controlled PR title. *Fix:* guard the job; or downgrade to `pull_request` since it only reads title/number.

**HIGH · `goap-assignment-router.yml:6, 30`** — `pull_request_target` with `ADMIN_GITHUB_TOKEN`, no fork guard. *Fix:* same as above.

**MEDIUM · `agent-fallback.yml:75-83`** — Uses `author_association == 'MEMBER' | 'OWNER' | 'COLLABORATOR'` which is the right shape — but `pull_request_target` also delivers `labeled` events; a malicious actor with triage rights cannot exploit it, yet `OPENHANDS_API_KEY`/`CURSOR_API_KEY`/`OPENROUTER_API_KEY` all enter env at line 97-99 *before* the gate filters. Workflow-level secrets are exposed; only the `run:` is gated. Acceptable but consider moving the association check to job-level `if:` (currently *is* on job — good — but verify `health-check` and `execute` both have it; `execute:` at line 148 has no `if:` and will run unconditionally when `health-check` completes). *Fix:* propagate the same guard to `execute:`.

**MEDIUM · `mergify-merge-queue-labels-copier.yml:13`** — `pull_request_target` with `if: startsWith(github.event.pull_request.head.ref, 'mergify/merge-queue/')`. A fork PR can name its head ref `mergify/merge-queue/anything`; the action then runs `Mergifyio/gha-mergify-merge-queue-labels-copier@v6` against it with `pull-requests: write`. *Fix:* add `&amp;&amp; github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository`.

**HIGH · `priority-router.yml`** — No `concurrency:` block. Triggers on five PR action types + 6-hourly cron. Push pileups will burn through `GITHUB_TOKEN` rate budget exactly as you observed. *Fix:* add `concurrency: { group: priority-router-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.run_id }}, cancel-in-progress: true }`.

**HIGH · `workflow-monitor.yml`** — 15-minute cron with no `concurrency:`; runs unbounded if previous run is slow. Heavy API user. *Fix:* `concurrency: { group: workflow-monitor, cancel-in-progress: false }` (don't cancel — coalesce).

**LOW · `docs-freshness-check.yml`** — Has `concurrency: cancel-in-progress: true` ✓ and uses `fetch-depth: 0` ✓ and `pull_request` (not `_target`) ✓. The earlier rate-limit failure this session was a fleet-wide GitHub installation token exhaustion, not this file. The fix is already present.

# WR/PR Pipeline Strict Review

## Top 5 Findings (a strict reviewer would refuse to merge)

### 1. Blocker — `wr/scripts/batch-generate-wrs.sh:59`
**What's wrong:** `batch-generate-wrs.sh` invokes the generator as `"$GENERATE_SCRIPT" "$repo_name"` (positional arg), but `generate-wr.sh:8-15` only accepts `--issue/--title/--body-file/--class/--meta` and exits 2 with `unknown arg $1` on anything else. The `echo "y" |` also implies an interactive prompt the new generator never had.
**Why it matters:** The "batch" path is dead code; anyone running `./batch-generate-wrs.sh p0` gets five red Xs and exit 1. If a green-path test ever exercises this it will silently pass because the failure is in a per-repo subshell — failed counter just increments. Mass-generation is documented but unsupported.
**Fix:** Either delete the script or rewrite it to call `generate-wr.sh --title "WR for $repo_name" --issue 0 --class basic` (and decide where the issue body/meta JSON comes from).

### 2. High — `.github/workflows/openrouter-coder.yml:33-36` (+ `openrouter_coder.py:46-54`)
**What's wrong:** The `issue_comment` trigger fires whenever `contains(github.event.comment.body, 'Research Findings:')` regardless of commenter identity (only `issue.user.login` is checked, not `comment.user.login`). Any drive-by commenter with read access can trigger a paid OpenRouter call that creates a PR. `validate_rel_path` rejects `..` and absolute paths but happily allows model-controlled writes to `.github/workflows/*.yml`, `.github/scripts/*.py`, `wr/scripts/wr-lint.mjs`, etc.
**Why it matters:** Untrusted-input → arbitrary CI/script overwrite → next workflow run executes attacker-controlled YAML/Python with `contents: write` and `pull-requests: write`. This is RCE on the CI runner with no human gate.
**Fix:** (a) Add `github.event.comment.author_association == 'OWNER' || 'MEMBER' || 'COLLABORATOR'` to the `if:`. (b) In `validate_rel_path`, deny any path under `.github/`, `wr/scripts/`, or matching `*.yml`/`*.yaml`/`*.sh`/`*.mjs` unless an explicit allowlist is provided. Pin `peter-evans/create-pull-request@v7` and `actions/checkout@v4` to commit SHAs like the other workflows do.

### 3. High — `.github/workflows/wr-lint.yml:26-34`
**What's wrong:** `files=$(git diff … 2&gt;&amp;1)` redirects stderr into the variable, and `node wr/scripts/wr-lint.mjs $files` is **unquoted**. A git warning ("warning: refname X is ambiguous") gets stored as "files" and passed as argv to `wr-lint.mjs`; or with no diff output and any non-zero pipeline upstream, the `|| files=""` only fires on git's own non-zero exit (git diff prints warnings without erroring). Also the gate is only triggered by `paths: ["wr/issues/**.md"]` — editing `wr-lint.mjs` itself never re-runs the lint on existing WRs.
**Why it matters:** (a) Silent CI passes when diff is unobtainable (PR from fork shallow clone; force-push; rename). (b) A change to the linter that introduces a regression ships without ever running against any sample WR. Combined with the `paths` filter on `fix-wr-gate.yml`, you can break both gates in a PR that touches only `wr/scripts/` and they won't fire.
**Fix:** Stop redirecting stderr into the var (`2&gt;/dev/null` or capture to a separate file). Quote the expansion: pass via `xargs -d '\n' -r node …` or read into a bash array. Add `wr/scripts/**`, `wr/WR_TEMPLATE_*.md`, and `.github/workflows/wr-*.yml` to the `paths` filter, and have the workflow lint a fixed set of golden-sample WRs whenever the linter itself changes.

### 4. High — `wr/scripts/fix-wr-gate.mjs:23-49` (escape hatches)
**What's wrong:** Two escape hatches:
- `TRACKING_PREFIXES` includes `/^track\b/i`, so a title like "Track down regression" or "Tracking failure cause" pattern-matches as tracking-only. Combine with `Tracks: #1` in the body (which the regex matches even inside a fenced code block, a blockquote, or a striked-out section) and the gate accepts a fake fix WR.
- `isRealFix("wr/...")` returns false for everything under `wr/`, so a real fix to `wr/scripts/wr-lint.mjs`, `wr/WR_TEMPLATE_BASIC.md`, etc. is treated as "WR-only" and blocked unless tracking-labeled. The gate punishes legitimate template/linter fixes.
**Why it matters:** Both directions of the gate are wrong — fake "tracking" PRs slip through, real template fixes get blocked into adopting the tracking label, which then teaches contributors to apply the escape-hatch label routinely.
**Fix:** Strip fenced blocks/blockquotes from `body` before `TRACKS_REF.test()`. Require `TRACKING_PREFIXES` to be the exact prefixes (`/^\[track\]/i`, `/^\[wr-tracking\]/i`) — drop the bare `/^track\b/i`. Exclude `wr/scripts/`, `wr/WR_TEMPLATE_*.md`, and `wr/README.md` from the `wr/`-only filter in `isRealFix`.

### 5. High — `wr/scripts/wr-lint.mjs:80-82` (raw-placeholder heuristic) and `:33-34` (token detector)
**What's wrong:** The "raw bracketed placeholder" rule is `/\[[A-Za-z][^\]]{2,60}\]/` after stripping markdown links and checkboxes. It will **false-positive** on legitimate content like `[Closes #123]`, `[TODO: refactor]`, `[RFC 2119]`, `[ticket ABC-12]`, footnote refs `[^1]` are fine but `[note 1]` triggers. Authors will start escaping or removing real prose to satisfy the gate. Meanwhile `RAW_TOKENS` is a fixed enum — any new generator token (`{REPO_URL}`, `{OWNER}`, `{LICENSE}`, etc.) silently passes the lint and the `sed` fallback in `generate-wr.sh:98` rewrites it to "N/A", erasing the bug.
**Why it matters:** Authors will route around the noisy linter; the token list goes out of sync with `generate-wr.sh`'s `subst …` calls and you ship `N/A` where data was supposed to land. Exactly the defect the gate was built to prevent.
**Fix:** Replace the heuristic with an allowlist of *known* template placeholders (read them out of `WR_TEMPLATE_FULL.md` / `WR_TEMPLATE_BASIC.md` at runtime). Detect unsubstituted tokens with a generic `\{[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*\}` rather than an enum, and remove the `sed -E 's/\{[A-Z_]+\}/N\/A/g'` fallback in `generate-wr.sh:98` so the lint actually catches missing substitutions instead of being papered over.

---

## Full list

### Medium

- **`wr/scripts/wr-lint.mjs:56-61`** — H1 detection misses setext form (`Title\n====`). Generator only emits ATX so probably fine today, but a hand-written WR with setext gets "no H1 header found" while clearly having one.
- **`wr/scripts/wr-lint.mjs:86`** — `BASIC_SIGNALS.test(path) || BASIC_SIGNALS.test(lines[0])`. If neither the path nor title contain a bug/fix word (e.g., title is "Remove unused MCP route"), the wrong-template-product-sections check is skipped — exactly the misclassification path the linter was built to catch.
- **`wr/scripts/generate-wr.sh:19`** — `ISSUE_BODY="$([[ -n "$BODY_FILE" &amp;&amp; -f "$BODY_FILE" ]] &amp;&amp; cat "$BODY_FILE" || echo "_No issue body provided._")"`. Classic `A &amp;&amp; B || C` bug: if `cat` ever fails (permission, race), `C` fires and the WR ships with the placeholder string regardless of `--body-file` being set. Use `if … then … else … fi`.
- **`wr/scripts/generate-wr.sh:71-95` + `:98`** — Subst order plus the final `sed` is unsafe under user input. Order: `ISSUE_BODY` is substituted before `STARS`/`SUMMARY`/etc., so if the issue body contains literal `{STARS}` or `{SUMMARY}` it gets *re-substituted* by later passes. Then the catch-all `sed -E 's/\{[A-Z_]+\}/N\/A/g'` chews any user-pasted `{ENV_VAR}` text in the body into `N/A`. Either escape `{` in user-substituted content or use a placeholder-only sentinel marker that doesn't collide with user text (e.g. `&lt;&lt;&lt;TOKEN&gt;&gt;&gt;`).
- **`.github/workflows/fix-wr-gate.yml:27`** — Triple-dot range `BASE_SHA...HEAD_SHA` differs from the two-arg form in `wr-lint.yml:26`. Pick one. Triple-dot from event-payload SHAs needs `git fetch` of base before it works on a freshly-checked-out PR (works here only because `fetch-depth: 0` was set; would silently break if anyone copy-pastes the workflow without depth 0).
- **`.github/workflows/no-root-junk.yml:34`** — Pattern only matches lowercase + a small extension list. `PLAN.md`, `Notes.md`, `plan.yml`, `plan.json`, `plan.tsx`, `TODO.md`, `draft.md` all slip past. Also `printf '%s\n' $JUNK` is unquoted; a renamed-into file containing spaces (rare) would word-split.
- **`wr/scripts/update-tracker.sh:66`** — `"**Total Repositories:** 140"` is hardcoded. Drifts the moment a repo is added. Compute from `gh repo list` or remove the line.
- **`wr/scripts/update-tracker.sh:28 vs 35`** — `TOTAL_WRS` uses recursive `find`; status counters use shallow glob `"$REPOS_DIR"/*.md`. The three counts won't sum to the total once subdirs exist, and an unrecognized status emoji (`🔵 Blocked`, `❌ Cancelled`) silently increments nothing.
- **`.github/workflows/openrouter-coder.yml:100`** — `eval "$ROO_RUN_COMMAND"` on a workspace variable is fine in principle, but the step exports `GITHUB_TOKEN` into its env at `:90` with `contents: write` and `pull-requests: write` job perms. Anyone who can edit org/repo vars (a wider set than secrets) can land an arbitrary command running with write tokens.

### Low

- **`wr/scripts/wr-lint.mjs:51`** — Fence detector `/^```/.test(l.trim())` toggles on the first ``` regardless of whether it's an opener with a language tag or a closer. Indented fences (4-space code blocks) are not detected at all; placeholders in those get flagged. Use a Markdown parser if accuracy matters.
- **`wr/scripts/fix-wr-gate.mjs:31`** — `--changed` is split on `,` and `\n`. Filenames with commas (legal in Git) split incorrectly. Use newline-only and document it.
- **`wr/scripts/generate-wr.sh:50`** — `jq_get` falls back to `echo ""` when `jq` is missing, so the whole template gets `N/A` for every field with no warning. At minimum, fail loud when jq is absent and a non-trivial `--meta` was passed.
- **`.github/workflows/wr-lint.yml:30-33`** — "no WR files changed; skipping lint" with `exit 0` means a force-push that wipes the diff range silently passes. Combine with finding #3 and you have a stealthy pass path.
- **`openrouter_coder.py:185`** — Default `commit_message = "feat: apply OpenRouter coding changes"` when the model returns a non-string. That's a `feat:` commit for what could be a doc/chore change; messes with semver/Changelog automation downstream.

### Tests-don't-test-the-failure-modes

No tests exist for `wr-lint.mjs` or `fix-wr-gate.mjs` in the repo (no `wr/scripts/__tests__/`, no `*.test.mjs`). Every regex above is unverified against the actual failing-WR patterns (#14227, #14186, #14185, #14138, #14118 etc.) the comments reference. A strict reviewer would refuse to ship a gate without at least 5-10 golden samples of "good" and "bad" WRs that fail/pass deterministically.

- The env-var hand-off in both workflows (`PR_TITLE`, `PR_BODY`, `PR_LABELS` via `env:` rather than direct `${{ }}` interpolation into `run:`) correctly avoids the standard GitHub Actions title-injection RCE pattern; this is good and rare to see done right.
- The non-global clone of `BRACKET_PLACEHOLDER` at `wr-lint.mjs:124` with the explanatory comment shows real awareness of the regex `lastIndex` gotcha — keep that pattern when adding new rules.</result>

## Pattern map

- **Half-fix / title-vs-diff drift (3 PRs)** — #14117, #14122, #13854 (Copilot's "potential fix for pull request finding" mini-commits stack 4 deep with no individual review). Title promises a code fix; diff is a doc/WR or unrelated YAML.
- **Tracking WR ships, real fix does not (≥4 PRs)** — #13978 (8 deferred items), #14117 (mcpPromptPack), #14122 (JSON audit), #13982 (566-line affiliate-engine WR, no engine code). Devin/Copilot keep stamping these "approved" because the diff is "non-risky markdown".
- **Scaffolding leaked to main (13 files)** — `# Otherwise, use WR_TEMPLATE_BASIC.md instead (recommended)` survived in WR issue files from `wr/issues/issue-13834-…` through `wr/issues/issue-14060-…`. The WR lint gate was only hardened on 2026-05-31 (commit `ef6f214`, `8dc6b85`); back-fill of the 13 dirty files never happened.
- **Unpinned third-party actions (4 newly-shipped workflows)** — `seo-a11y-guard.yml`, `spec-approval-gate.yml`, `conflict-helper.yml` (`checkout@v4`), `recovery-engine.yml` (`github-script@v9.0.0`). All landed AFTER the third-party-action audit (#13993) and AFTER `workflow-action-ref-audit.yml` was added to the repo.
- **Workflow check disabled / advisory (2 PRs)** — `cypress-lead-engine.yml` `continue-on-error: true` (#13972), `mabl.yml` triggers commented out (#13967). If `mabl` is in branch-protection required checks, paused PRs will be stuck until it's removed there too — not addressed in the PR.
- **Default-token assumption (2 PRs)** — #14092 and #14101 both write/label expecting downstream workflows to refire; default `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot do this. Documented self-healing behavior will not actually self-heal.
- **Secret/token misuse (1 PR)** — `scripts/secret-set.sh:33,56` accepts the secret as a positional CLI arg, exposing it via shell history and `ps aux`. Stdin should be the only path for a "secret-set" tool.
- **Provenance violation (1 PR)** — #14068 adds `@octp/cli` (unverifiable package) plus a `pull_request_target` block in the same PR that "applies the provenance standard."

## Devin's blind spots

Devin systematically waves through any PR where the diff is "safe-looking text" — markdown WR docs, label-handling try/catch wraps, comment additions, and `if:` guards that silence rather than fix. It does not cross-check the PR title against the diff, so commits titled `fix: …` that only ship a tracking document slip through (#14117, #14122). It also gives a pass to "shipped-but-marked-temporary" hacks (`continue-on-error: true`, `--legacy-peer-deps`, commented-out triggers) because they're labeled as transitional in the commit body, even when no follow-up issue exists. Finally, Devin does not enforce this repo's own newly-landed standards against the same PR set — unpinned `@v4` actions, `pull_request_target` additions, and `@octp/cli`-style unverified packages all merged while the Provenance Standard, third-party-action audit, and `workflow-action-ref-audit.yml` sat in the same tree. The net pattern: Devin trusts intent statements in commit bodies over what the diff actually does, and over what the repo's own gates already say.

When that happens today, Ralph posts \"\ud83d\udd04 Ralph Loop \u2014 Attempt N/5\" comments on closed PRs and tries to push fix commits to already-merged branches.\n\nWe came close to watching this thrash on #14254 in the previous session.\n\n## Fix\n\nGuard the trigger condition with a PR-state check:\n\n```yaml\nif: |\n  github.event.check_suite.conclusion == 'failure' &&\n  (github.event.check_suite.pull_requests[0] == null ||\n   github.event.check_suite.pull_requests[0].state == 'open')\n```\n\n- `pull_requests[0] == null` keeps manual (non-PR) check_suite runs working.\n- `state == 'open'` skips merged/closed PRs.\n\n## Verified\n\nGitHub's `check_suite` payload `.pull_requests[*].state` is documented to be one of `open|closed`. Closed PRs (both merged and abandoned) return `closed`.\n\n## Notes\n\nOne of nine cleanup PRs from the strict-reviewer audit. The Ralph self-healing loop still works on every genuinely-open PR \u2014 the only behavior change is that it stops firing on closed/merged ones.",

  "title": "ralph-loop: skip merged/closed PRs (state guard)"
}

**Impact:** A file path like `/docs/fix-something/file.md` might incorrectly trigger BASIC classification

**Issue:** The allowlist captures all `[...]` brackets from templates, which might include legitimate prose

```

### Step 3: Monitor template allowlist behavior (P2)
No immediate action needed, but consider adding validation that template placeholders are actually meant to be preserved.

### 🧠 thinking

## 🤖 assistant

The "Promote Draft PR When CI Passes" workflow needs a token that can call GitHub's `markPullRequestReadyForReview` GraphQL mutation. It tries three in order:

1. **`READY_FOR_REVIEW_TOKEN`** — a dedicated PAT you'd create as `oaudrey` (or another admin user). Not set in your repo.
2. **`ADMIN_GITHUB_TOKEN`** — your admin PAT. Probably set, but if it's expired, scoped wrong, or hit rate limit, it falls through.
3. **Default `GITHUB_TOKEN`** — the auto-provisioned token that runs every workflow as `github-actions[bot]`. GitHub deliberately blocks this token from "marking ready," because that action would trigger more workflows and could create infinite loops.

So in practice it has to be #2. The failure means either:
- `ADMIN_GITHUB_TOKEN` isn't set, OR
- It's set but doesn't have `pull_requests: write` on this repo, OR
- It's the same PAT hitting the per-user 5,000 req/hr ceiling (the rate-limit we saw earlier)

Cheapest verification: run `gh secret list -R midnghtsapphire/revvel-standards | grep ADMIN_GITHUB_TOKEN` (or check the repo's Settings → Secrets). If it's there and unexpired, it's just throttled — comes back next hour. If it's missing or expired, generate a fresh fine-grained PAT scoped only to this repo with `pull_requests: write` and `contents: read`, set it as `ADMIN_GITHUB_TOKEN`, and the auto-promote starts working on every PR.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# gatekeeper-rotate.sh — Check and execute secret rotations based on the Gatekeeper registry.
#
# Reads docs/_GATEKEEPER_REGISTRY.json, finds entries past their next_rotation
# date, and either auto-rotates (if the provider supports it) or creates a
# GitHub issue prompting manual rotation.
#
# Usage:
#   bash scripts/gatekeeper-rotate.sh --check          # Dry-run: show what's due
#   bash scripts/gatekeeper-rotate.sh --execute         # Actually rotate + log
#   bash scripts/gatekeeper-rotate.sh --warn-days 7     # Warn about upcoming rotations
#
# Environment:
#   DOPPLER_TOKEN   Service token with read/write access
#   GITHUB_TOKEN    For creating issues (set on Actions runners)
#   DRY_RUN=1       Print actions without executing

set -euo pipefail

REGISTRY_FILE="docs/_GATEKEEPER_REGISTRY.json"
ROTATION_LOG="docs/_ROTATION_LOG.md"
MODE="check"
WARN_DAYS=7
DRY_RUN="${DRY_RUN:-0}"

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --check) MODE="check"; shift ;;
    --execute) MODE="execute"; shift ;;
    --warn-days)
      [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { echo "error: --warn-days requires a value" >&2; exit 2; }
      WARN_DAYS="$2"; shift 2 ;;

## 🤖 assistant

Found the culprit. You've got **a hourly cron workflow that overwrites secrets every 60 minutes**:

**`.github/workflows/secret-persistence-guard.yml`** (runs `cron: 0 * * * *` = every hour):

1. Checks if `ADMIN_GITHUB_TOKEN`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, `JULES_API_KEY`, etc. are "missing"
2. If anything's missing → pulls from Doppler API → runs `gh secret set ADMIN_GITHUB_TOKEN --body "$VALUE"` — **overwriting whatever you just set**

The "missing" check is `[ -z "$value" ]` (empty string). The failure mode that's likely killing you:

- You set fresh `ADMIN_GITHUB_TOKEN` via GitHub UI at, say, 2:15pm
- 3:00pm cron fires
- Workflow reads `secrets.ADMIN_GITHUB_TOKEN` → if anything in the propagation chain returns empty (caching, GitHub Actions secret-context resolution glitch, etc.), it's flagged "missing"
- Auto-recover pulls **Doppler's stale value** (probably the OLD expired PAT you put there originally)
- `gh secret set` overwrites your fresh token with the stale one
- Next time anything tries to use it: "Bad credentials" / 401 / promote-draft fails

Plus two scheduled-rotation workflows that actively delete-and-recreate secrets on Mondays:
- **`secret-rotation-schedule.yml`** — Mon 2am UTC
- **`gatekeeper-rotate.yml`** — Mon 6am UTC

Both check rotation metadata (`wr/memory/secret-rotations.md` / `docs/_GATEKEEPER_REGISTRY.json`) and rotate if past due. If `ADMIN_GITHUB_TOKEN` is listed there with a 30/60-day rotation, they'll nuke it on schedule.

**Immediate stop-the-bleed:** disable the hourly workflow until you confirm Doppler has the CORRECT current value of each protected secret. One PR:

```yaml
# .github/workflows/secret-persistence-guard.yml
on:
  # schedule:                          # ← comment out
  #   - cron: 0 * * * *
  workflow_dispatch:                   # keep manual trigger
    inputs:
      force_recovery: ...
```

Want me to open that PR? Also worth grepping `wr/memory/secret-rotations.md` to see if your tokens are scheduled to auto-rotate weekly — that'd explain the second-order disappearances.

**Cluster 1 ("🚨 Secrets Missing")** — this is `secrets-sentinel.yml` and `secret-persistence-guard.yml` running on cron, false-positiving on "missing" secrets (Doppler returns stale → context resolution glitches → marked missing → spam issue), creating a new issue every hour for *each* "missing" secret. **Copilot's "3,319 open issues"** is mostly self-inflicted noise from these two workflows. Bulk-closing them by hand is impossible; the fix is stopping the source first, then bulk-closing the duplicates.

Recommended sequence:

1. **Stop the bleed** — disable cron on `secret-persistence-guard.yml`, `secrets-sentinel.yml`, and the audit-logger workflow. One small PR.
2. **Bulk-close the noise** — close all issues matching `🚨 Secrets Missing` and `[FAILURE] Agent Audit Logger failed` with a single bot comment ("auto-closed: workflow disabled in PR #X"). Either via the GitHub UI (search → select-all → close) or a one-shot script.
3. **Then** the 9 cleanup PRs land and you can deal with the real backlog.

## 🤖 assistant

Quick clarification — Octopus can't read your GitHub repo secrets even when they're there. Repo secrets only decrypt inside GitHub Actions runs that you authorize; the Octopus GitHub App has no access to them (GitHub doesn't expose secrets to third-party apps, by design).

When Octopus says *"add your own API keys in Settings"*, they mean **Octopus's own settings UI** at their dashboard (likely `octopus-review.ai/settings` or `/dashboard/settings`). That's where you paste an Octopus/OpenAI/Anthropic/OpenRouter key that Octopus's backend then uses to power your reviews — billed against your key, not their pool.

So:
- ✅ Key in repo secrets — useful for *your* workflows that need it
- ❌ Key in repo secrets — does **nothing** for Octopus's review pass

Path forward: log in at https://octopus-review.ai, find the BYOK / API key field in your org settings, paste an OpenRouter or Anthropic key there. Once saved, Octopus's review will resume on your remaining PRs this cycle.

You're right — I had it wrong. Let me correct:

There are **two Octopus surfaces**, and they bill differently:

1. **Octopus Review GitHub App** (`octopus-review[bot]`) — the SaaS bot that posts review comments. Runs on Octopus's servers. **This one** is hitting your org's monthly limit. Adding `OCTOPUS_TOKEN` to repo secrets does NOT help this lane — it's billed via Octopus's dashboard.

2. **Octopus CLI** (`.github/workflows/octopus-cli.yml`) — runs *inside* your GitHub Actions, calls `octopus login --token "$OCTOPUS_TOKEN"`, then runs `octopus review` on the PR. **This one DOES read `OCTOPUS_TOKEN` from repo secrets** — exactly what Octopus's docs told you. This is your independent lane, billed against your own Octopus account/credits.

So if you put `OCTOPUS_TOKEN` in repo secrets (which you did), the CLI lane should run on every PR and post reviews even when the SaaS bot is rate-limited.

**Current state:** the CLI lane is broken on main right now — `octopus-cli.yml` has the duplicate `invoke:` job key bug we caught in the audit. **PR #14373 fixes it.** Once that merges, your in-repo Octopus reviews resume automatically using the token in repo secrets. The bot's rate-limit message becomes mostly irrelevant.

So: the key IS in the right place, the lane is just blocked by an unmerged fix. Want me to push #14373 to the front of the merge queue?

🚩 **Escalate job condition may fire when auto-recover is skipped**

In `secret-persistence-guard.yml:303`, the `escalate` job uses `if: always() &amp;&amp; needs.auto-recover.outputs.failed != '[]'`. When the `schedule` trigger is disabled and only `workflow_dispatch` triggers the workflow, the `auto-recover` job may be skipped (if `monitor-secret-health` reports no missing secrets). When a job is skipped, its outputs are empty strings. The condition `'' != '[]'` evaluates to `true`, which means the escalate job would run even when auto-recover was skipped (no missing secrets). However, this is a pre-existing issue not introduced by this PR — it existed before the cron was commented out and would trigger identically via `workflow_dispatch`. The practical impact is low because the `escalate` step would then try to parse empty `FAILED_SECRETS` and `RECOVERED_SECRETS` env vars, likely producing a malformed but mostly empty issue.

*(Refers to line 303)*

🟡 **Unescaped backticks in heredoc trigger shell command substitution**

Lines 373 and 378 use raw backticks around `workflow_dispatch` inside an unquoted `&lt;&lt;EOF` heredoc. In bash, unescaped backticks in an unquoted heredoc are interpreted as command substitution — bash will try to execute `workflow_dispatch` as a shell command, which doesn't exist. This replaces the text with an empty string and emits `bash: workflow_dispatch: command not found` to stderr. Every other backtick in this same heredoc is properly escaped (e.g., `\`CREDENTIAL_BACKUP_JSON\`` on line 375, `\`\`\`bash` on line 342, etc.).

The resulting GitHub issue body will show mangled text like `— run  manually to re-check` and `run this workflow via ` with the word `workflow_dispatch` silently removed.

Comment: <untrusted_external_data source="pr_comment">&lt;!-- devin-review-comment &#123;"id": "ANALYSIS_pr-review-job-d408bf2a3a2c4653990c43a33b7c6acc_0001", "file_path": ".github/workflows/secret-persistence-guard.yml", "start_line": 303, "end_line": 303, "side": "RIGHT"&#125; --&gt;

📝 **Info: Escalate job condition change correctly prevents false-positive escalation**

The old condition at `secret-persistence-guard.yml:303` was `always() &amp;&amp; needs.auto-recover.outputs.failed != '[]'`. When `auto-recover` is skipped (because `monitor-secret-health` found no missing secrets), its outputs are empty strings, not `'[]'`. Since `'' != '[]'` evaluates to `true` in GitHub Actions expressions, the old code would fire the escalate job even when there were no missing secrets — creating a spurious issue with empty `FAILED_SECRETS`. The new condition adds `needs.auto-recover.result != 'skipped'`, which correctly short-circuits before evaluating the outputs. This is a valid bugfix.

**On your quota question:** plausibly yes, partial cause. Two ways it could have contributed to the hallucination:

1. **Cached state.** When Devin hits monthly quota, the GitHub App may degrade to serving a cached prior review state — referring to a commit it saw earlier on a *different* PR. Doesn't quite fit here though (the SHA `712a3e1` didn't appear on *any* PR in this session — I checked).

2. **Degraded sampling.** Some agents fall back to cheaper/smaller models when a quota tier is exhausted. Smaller models hallucinate plausible-looking commit SHAs more often when reasoning about repo state they can't actually see.

Honest take: **the hallucination is more likely just standard LLM behavior than quota-caused.** LLMs invent plausible 7-char hex strings as "evidence" all the time, especially when generating self-referential "✅ Resolved" follow-ups where they're trying to close a thread cleanly. The way to know for sure would be to check Devin's app dashboard for the request log on PR #14436 — if there's a session with no actual file-diff inspection step but a "Resolved" comment posted, that's the smoking gun.

Either way, the doc I just shipped captures the lesson regardless of cause: **verify Devin's "✅ Resolved" claims against actual git log before trusting them.**

## 🤖 assistant

Probably not — but related. `admin:org` is a different scope.

For the `markPullRequestReadyForReview` mutation that's failing on these PRs:
- **Classic PAT** needs the `repo` scope (covers all repo-level writes, including marking PRs ready)
- **Fine-grained PAT** needs `Pull requests: Write` on the target repo

`admin:org` controls org-level admin (teams, members, org webhooks, billing). A PAT with **only** `admin:org` would NOT be able to mark a PR ready — it'd hit the same permission-denied / 401 you're seeing.

So if you generated `ADMIN_GITHUB_TOKEN` with just `admin:org` (because that's what something else asked for), that explains the failure pattern across all the cleanup PRs.

**Fix:** regenerate the PAT with both scopes:
- ✅ `repo` (the one that covers PR-ready and most repo operations)
- ✅ `admin:org` (keep, since other workflows depend on it)
- Optionally `workflow` (if any workflow writes to `.github/workflows/`)

Or — cleaner if you're on fine-grained PATs — set:
- `Repository permissions → Pull requests: Read and write`
- `Repository permissions → Contents: Read and write`
- `Organization permissions → Members: Read` (only if you actually need org-level)

Want me to also amend the Devin observations doc (the wrong-framing thing from your last message)?

## 🤖 assistant

OK that rules out scope. The remaining culprits (in order of likelihood for this repo specifically):

1. **Your own workflow overwriting it.** `secret-persistence-guard.yml` runs hourly and pulls `ADMIN_GITHUB_TOKEN` from Doppler with `gh secret set`. If Doppler has the *old* expired value, the workflow overwrites your freshly-set full-scope token with the stale one — even though your new token had every permission. **PR #14436 disables this loop**; that single merge probably ends the "tokens disappear" pattern.

2. **GitHub secret scanning auto-revocation.** If any token *ever* shows up in a workflow log line (an `echo $VAR`, a `curl -v` printing auth headers, a debug step), GitHub auto-revokes it within minutes. The full-rights scoping doesn't protect against this — actually makes it more aggressive because GitHub knows a leaked admin token is high-value. Worth checking GitHub's "Security log" → "Tokens" tab for revocation events.

3. **SAML SSO authorization.** If your org requires SAML SSO, every new PAT needs an explicit "Authorize SAML" click on the token page *after* generation. Without that step, even a fully-scoped token returns "Resource not accessible by integration" against repos in the SSO-required org. PAT works fine in personal repos, fails in the org-required one.

4. **Token expiration.** Fine-grained PATs default to **90 days** unless you change it; classic PATs can be "no expiration" but that option is increasingly restricted.

Given you've already burned a day on this — the highest-impact move is **landing PR #14436 first** to stop the overwrite loop. Then set a fresh PAT, check it works once, and observe whether it stays. ## 🧑 user

so is doppler disabled or commented out now? i thought we were using the backup anyway

### 🧠 thinking

> 

## 🤖 assistant

Good catch. **No — Doppler is NOT disabled by PR #14436.** Only the *hourly cron* is paused. Doppler integration is still wired throughout the workflow:

- `secret-persistence-guard.yml` still uses `DOPPLER_TOKEN` env var
- `secrets-sentinel.yml` still uses it
- If anyone manually triggers either via `workflow_dispatch`, Doppler is called FIRST, and the backup harness only runs as fallback for whatever Doppler didn't return

So even with the cron paused, the moment someone clicks "Run workflow" the Doppler-overwrite path is back open.

If you're actually using `CREDENTIAL_BACKUP_JSON` as your source of truth, the cleanest fix is to make Doppler stop being primary. Three options:

1. **Unset `DOPPLER_TOKEN` (and the aliases) from repo secrets** — easy, no code change. The `DOPPLER_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DOPPLER_AGENT_TOKEN || secrets.DOPPLER_TOKEN || secrets.DOPPLER_LOCAL_TOKEN || secrets.DOPPLER_API_KEY || secrets.DOPPLER_AGENT_ODIC || secrets.DOPPLER_CIRCLECI_OIDC }}` chain resolves to empty → Doppler step short-circuits with `"No Doppler token available — skipping Doppler recovery"` → backup harness runs instead. Reversible by re-setting the secret.

2. **Swap order in the workflow** — patch `secret-persistence-guard.yml` so backup harness runs first, Doppler only as fallback. ~10-line change.

3. **Rip Doppler out entirely** — delete the Doppler branch from both workflows. Aggressive but cleanest if you're not using it anywhere.

Want me to extend PR #14436 to do option 2 (backup-first ordering)? That'd actually finish the "stop the bleed" fix instead of just pausing the cron.

## 🧑 user

so you need a classic and fine grained pat?

### 🧠 thinking

> 

## 🤖 assistant

No — pick **one**, not both. They're alternatives, not stacked layers.

| | Classic PAT | Fine-grained PAT |
|---|---|---|
| Scopes | Broad (`repo`, `admin:org`, `workflow`, etc.) | Per-permission per-repo |
| Repo targeting | All-or-nothing — token works on every repo you own | Pick specific repos |
| Expiration | Can be "no expiration" | Defaults 90 days, max 1 year |
| Setup | One token covers everything | More fields to configure |
| Risk if leaked | High (all repos) | Lower (just the repos you allowed) |

For **your situation** (one repo, lots of automation, you already give max scopes anyway):

→ **Classic PAT with `repo` + `workflow` + `admin:org`** is what I'd use. One token, no expiration if you can keep it that way, covers everything the cleanup chain needs.

The fine-grained route is "safer in theory" but you'd be re-generating it every 90 days, which is exactly the "burn a day on tokens" pain you're already in.

So: one classic PAT, full rights, no expiration, set it as `ADMIN_GITHUB_TOKEN`. Done.

Two ways to stop the bleed **right now** without waiting for the PR:

1. **Disable the workflow directly in the GitHub UI** (fastest): Settings → Actions → "Secret Persistence Guard" → ⋯ menu → Disable workflow. Same for "Secrets Sentinel". Doesn't require any code change; takes effect immediately. You can re-enable any time.

2. **Unset Doppler tokens from repo secrets**: Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → delete `DOPPLER_TOKEN`, `DOPPLER_AGENT_TOKEN`, `DOPPLER_LOCAL_TOKEN`, `DOPPLER_API_KEY`, `DOPPLER_AGENT_ODIC`, `DOPPLER_CIRCLECI_OIDC`. PR: midnghtsapphire/revvel-standards#14436
Author: midnghtsapphire
Comment: <untrusted_external_data source="pr_comment">@cursoragent please fix: 📝 Info: Escalate job condition change correctly prevents false-positive escalation

The old condition at secret-persistence-guard.yml:303 was always() &amp;&amp; needs.auto-recover.outputs.failed != '[]'. When auto-recover is skipped (because monitor-secret-health found no missing secrets), its outputs are empty strings, not '[]'. Since '' != '[]' evaluates to true in GitHub Actions expressions, the old code would fire the escalate job even when there were no missing secrets — creating a spurious issue with empty FAILED_SECRETS. The new condition adds needs.auto-recover.result != 'skipped', which correctly short-circuits before evaluating the outputs. This is a valid bugfix.

Open in Devin Review

Yes — what you're describing is the right shape. Let me lock the design in concrete terms:

**Module contract** (one folder per agent):
```
modules/agents/{name}/
  module.yaml      ← name, lane, secret, cost_usd_mo, ttl_seconds
  status.sh        ← exit 0 ok | 65 no_credits | 66 rate_limited | 67 no_secret
  invoke.sh        ← reads STDIN prompt, writes JSON result to STDOUT
  cost.sh          ← returns {spent_mo, limit_mo, remaining_mo}
```

**Lanes registry** (one file maps purpose → fallback chain):
```yaml
# config/lanes.yml
coder:    [openrouter-coder, cursor, devin, openhands]
diagnose: [devin, openrouter-triage]
recover:  [credential-backup-harness, doppler]
review:   [octopus-cli, copilot, cubic, coderabbit]
```

**Orchestrator** (one CLI replaces all the bespoke `if: secrets.X != ''` gating):
```
agents call coder --prompt "..."
  → reads lanes.yml
  → tries modules in order, skips ones whose status.sh exited non-zero
  → returns first success
agents status-all     ← cached 5min, shows green/yellow/red + remaining credit per agent
agents cost           ← totals enabled modules' monthly burn
agents enable devin   ← flips module.yaml's enabled flag
```

**Recursive aspect**: a lane is itself a module. `coder` lane can appear in another lane's fallback chain. So `review` lane could include `coder` as its last resort. No special casing.

**Token-economy wins**:
- Status cached 5min → 12 PR events / hour → 1 status call / hour per agent, not 60
- Lane fan-out gated by PR-risk label → small PRs only call free lanes; only blocker-class fans out to paid
- One workflow consumes `agents call` instead of 10 workflows hardcoding individual SDKs → less surface to maintain

5. Status cache at `/tmp/agent-status-cache.json`

Total: ~600 lines, half-day. Doesn't touch the other 18 workflows until Phase 2.

Heard. Stop band-aiding. Build the spine right.

Here's what reads as **A System** — every piece is essential, removing any one of them turns it back into bash glue:

**1. Contract** (`docs/AGENT_MODULE_CONTRACT.md` + `schemas/agent-module.schema.json`)
   - Typed `module.yaml` — capabilities, domains, complexity range, cost per call, monthly cap, fallback chain
   - Typed status output, typed invoke input/output
   - JSON Schema validation enforced in CI; module that fails the schema can't load

**2. Modules** (`modules/agents/{name}/`)
   - Same shape for all 30 — Devin, OpenRouter, Doppler, CodeRabbit, etc. all look identical
   - Declared, not implied — what the module CAN do is data, not "you have to read the bash to know"

**3. Engines** (`engines/`)
   - `classifier/` — extracts task features: type (code/research/review/recover), complexity (LOC/file estimate), domain (auth/db/CI/docs), risk tier
   - `router/` — scores enabled modules against task features + budget remaining + recent reliability; picks top
   - `cost-ledger/` — every invocation logged with module/cost/latency/outcome; budget caps fed back to router
   - `health-cache/` — module status TTL'd (5min), so we're not paying 12 PR events × 30 modules in status pings

**4. Lanes** (`config/lanes.yml`)
   - Declarative purposes: `coder`, `review`, `recover`, `diagnose`, `research`
   - Each lane lists eligible modules + fan-out rules + budget cap per call

**5. CLI + MCP** (`scripts/agents` and `mcp/agent-orchestrator/`)
   - `agents call <lane> --task-file <md>` — orchestrator decides which module, returns result + metadata
   - `agents status-all` / `agents cost` / `agents enable/disable`
   - MCP server exposes the same operations as tools — AI assistants can manage the fleet without bash

**6. Tests** (`tests/agent-system/`)
   - Fixture tasks with `expected_route` annotations
   - Golden routing tests: "this kind of task should go to module X first, Y as fallback"
   - Contract conformance tests for every module

**7. Standards doc** (`docs/AGENT_SYSTEM_STANDARD.md`)
   - The one-page spec contributors read. References the contract. Adding a 31st module is a checklist, not archaeology.

**LLM weighting in the router** — exactly your ask:
- Classifier extracts task signals

# Project Dashboard System

**Centralized visibility into all MIDNGHTSAPPHIRE projects, BOM, inventory, test URLs, and status**

## Problem Statement

No visibility into:
- BOM (Bill of Materials) inventory across projects
- Handoff documents and project status
- Test URLs scattered in folders
- Domain implementations and status
- Project confusion (which projects exist, where they are, what status)
- Overall project tracking without "looking in folders"

## Solution

A comprehensive **Project Dashboard System** that:

1. **Aggregates** all project data from multiple sources
2. **Generates** a centralized HTML dashboard and JSON data file
3. **Automates** updates via GitHub Actions cron job (hourly)
4. **Provides** CLI tool for quick access without opening files
5. **Tracks** projects, URLs, domains, inventory, and BOM in one place

---

open dashboard.html         # Open in browser
```

Or use the CLI:

```bash

=== wr/NORTH_STAR.md (head) ===
# WR North Star

Rules above all other rules. Audrey can override any of them.

## The Revvel Rule (Labor Must Be Paid)
Every project must, within a defined timeline, pay Audrey Evans for her labor. A project that can't define how it pays Audrey goes to Not Now. "I'll figure out monetization later" is a blocker, not a plan. Every repo must answer: "Who pays, how much, starting when?"

## The Paperwork Conservation Principle
Paperwork already correctly filed is an asset. Any agent proposing a change to a legally-filed record MUST document: (1) concrete upside, (2) worst-case failure, (3) is there a path that achieves the same outcome WITHOUT touching the filed record? If (3) exists, take (3).

## The Consistency Exemption
Perfect consistency across IRS, SOS, SAM.gov, Play Store, etc. is NOT required. Each record only needs to be correct for its own purpose. Drift is normal. WR tracks drift for visibility, not for forced correction.

## The Sequencing Rule (Revenue Before Mission)
Revenue projects are prioritized above mission projects until portfolio produces ≥$3,000/mo to Audrey. Mission without funding burns out the mission-holder. Audrey's own survival is the mission's first line item.

## The Principal Authority Rule
Audrey is the final authority. Agents may propose, warn, push back — but Audrey's informed instinct overrides analysis. No agent may re-litigate a decision Audrey has locked.

## The Durability Rule
This repo is the single source of truth. All critical data lives in plain markdown — readable by any human, any tool, any century. The repo is designed to outlive the tools that created it.

## The Commit Cadence Rule
Many small merged PRs > large unmerged ones. Audrey's operational security depends on visible accumulated progress. Never let a PR grow beyond one day's work before merging.

## The Quiet Mode Default
This system ships with automation OFF. Nothing runs on cron until Audrey opens an issue titled `exit-quiet-mode`. Silence is the default.

Automated PDF generation directly from GitHub Work Requests unlocks scalable, passive revenue pipelines. Codifying the batch sizes (1, 3, or 20) directly in the issue form standardizes the hand-off to external workflow engines like Make.com, eliminating manual intervention and human error associated with ad-hoc labeling.

- GitHub Actions Documentation: Webhook integrations

| Manual PDF Generation | Bespoke formatting | High labor cost | High |
| Traditional Automation | Unstructured webhook triggers | Variable | Medium |

#### Gaps in Existing Solutions

1. **Gap 1:** Unreliable label-based triggers in CI.

2. **Gap 2:** Lack of batching for output generation.

# Closed-PR Audit: `midnghtsapphire/revvel-standards` — search `pdf OR gumloop OR sellable OR n8n`

## Headline numbers
- **Total closed PRs matching the search: 9** (this is the entire result set; `total_count: 9, incomplete_results: false`).

The premise that "agents/automation are closing PRs without merging and losing scoped work" is **not supported by this dataset**. 7 of 9 PRs landed cleanly; only 2 were closed unmerged, and both were closed within minutes/hours of being opened by the author.

## state_reason / who closed them
**The GitHub Search API does not return a `closed_by` field on PR items.** The available keys per item are: `assignee, assignees, author_association, body, closed_at, comments, ..., pull_request{diff_url, html_url, merged_at, patch_url, url}, state, title, updated_at, user`. So "who closed it" cannot be answered from this file alone — you'd need `gh api repos/midnghtsapphire/revvel-standards/pulls/{n}` or the issue-events endpoint for each PR.

`state_reason` is **`null` on all 9 PRs** (GitHub generally only populates `state_reason` for issues — "completed"/"not_planned"/"reopened" — not for PRs). So no "duplicate", "stale", or "spam" reason was set on any of them; that's GitHub's data model, not evidence of automation.

# USDA Loan & Packager Deep Research — Master Reference

**Research Date:** April 30, 2026  
**Research Agent:** GitHub Copilot Coding Agent  
**Requested By:** @midnghtsapphire  
**Issue:** [WR] AGENT FOR USDA LOANS AND A THING CALLED PACKAGERS  
**Scope:** USDA Section 502 loans, loan packager regulations, property eligibility, income limits, state variations, legal loopholes, automation opportunities

---

## Executive Summary

This research covers the complete USDA Rural Development loan ecosystem, including:
- **USDA Section 502 Guaranteed & Direct Loan Programs** — 100% financing for rural homebuyers
- **Loan Packagers** — Third-party professionals who prepare and submit USDA loan applications
- **Property Eligibility** — Rural area definitions, inground pool restrictions, square footage misconceptions
- **Income Limits** — State-by-state, county-by-county adjusted limits (2026 data)
- **State Licensing Variations** — MLO license requirements by state for packagers
- **Legal Loopholes** — NEMT → utility → special district → police powers (historical + current alternatives)
- **Automation Opportunities** — SaaS platform model, n8n workflows, API integrations

**Key Finding:** USDA loans allow 100% financing with NO down payment for low-to-moderate income buyers in rural areas. Loan packagers can earn $500-$2,500 per closed loan paid by lenders (not borrowers). State licensing varies widely — some states require NMLS MLO license, others have no regulation.

**Automation Potential:** HIGH — A TurboTax-style SaaS platform for USDA loan preparation is legally permissible and could serve underserved rural markets. Direct API integration with USDA/lenders may trigger MLO licensing in some states.

---

# The Ultimate Guide for Hotel Professionals: Navigating the Industry

## Introduction

The hospitality industry is fast-paced, demanding, and incredibly rewarding. For hotel workers—ranging from front desk agents and concierges to housekeeping and management—the ability to adapt, provide exceptional service, and manage stress is crucial. This comprehensive guide provides actionable strategies, professional development tips, and best practices to excel in your hospitality career.

## 1. Mastering the Front of House

The front desk is the face of the hotel. First impressions matter immensely.

* **Proactive Problem Solving:** Anticipate guest needs before they arise. If a flight is delayed, have recommendations ready for local dining or activities.
* **Effective Communication:** Clear, concise, and empathetic communication is key. Use positive language even when delivering difficult news.
* **De-escalation Techniques:** When dealing with an upset guest, remember the LAST method: Listen, Apologize, Solve, and Thank. Let them express their frustration without interrupting.

## 2. Excellence in Housekeeping

Housekeeping is the backbone of guest satisfaction. A clean room is a non-negotiable expectation.

* **Efficiency and Attention to Detail:** Develop a systematic approach to cleaning to maximize efficiency without sacrificing quality. Always double-check high-touch areas like remotes and light switches.
* **Time Management:** Prioritize tasks based on check-ins, check-outs, and stay-overs. Use a checklist to ensure nothing is missed.
* **Health and Safety First:** Always use proper lifting techniques and be mindful of chemical interactions when using cleaning supplies.

## 3. The Art of the Concierge

A great concierge curates experiences, not just reservations.

* **Deep Local Knowledge:** Go beyond the tourist traps. Cultivate relationships with local business owners to offer exclusive recommendations.
* **Personalization:** Pay attention to guest preferences (e.g., dietary restrictions, interests) to tailor your suggestions.
* **Networking:** Build a strong network of contacts in the local dining, entertainment, and transportation sectors.

'use strict';

// Subscription & repository tracker.
//
// Reads data/subscriptions.yml (the SSOT inventory of paid/trial third-party
// tools, GitHub Apps and SaaS) and computes, per entry, how close it is to a
// trial expiry or a renewal charge — so a trial like RecurseML's 14-day window
// never lapses silently or auto-converts to a paid plan unnoticed.
//
// Everything here is pure and clock-injectable so the logic is unit-testable;
// the workflow (.github/workflows/subscription-tracker.yml) wires it to GitHub.

const fs = require('fs');
const path = require('path');
const YAML = require('yaml');

// Default warning window: surface anything due within this many days.
const DEFAULT_WARN_WITHIN_DAYS = 7;

// Where the SSOT lives, relative to the repo root.
const DEFAULT_SUBSCRIPTIONS_FILE = path.join('data', 'subscriptions.yml');

const MS_PER_DAY = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;

// Parse a YYYY-MM-DD string into a UTC timestamp at midnight. Returns null for
// missing/invalid input so callers can treat the due-date as "unknown".
function parseDate(dateStr) {
  if (!dateStr) return null;
  const value = String(dateStr).trim();
  if (!/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/.test(value)) return null;
  const ms = Date.parse(`${value}T00:00:00Z`);
  return Number.isNaN(ms) ? null : ms;
}

// Whole days from `now` until `dateStr` (negative = already past). null when the
// date is missing/unparseable.
function daysUntil(dateStr, now = Date.now()) {
  const target = parseDate(dateStr);
  if (target == null) return null;
  return Math.ceil((target - now) / MS_PER_DAY);

=== SUBSCRIPTION_TRACKER.md (head) ===
# Subscription & Trial Tracker

A lightweight, self-maintaining job that tracks every paid (or trial) third-party
tool, GitHub App, and SaaS used across MIDNGHTSAPPHIRE / Revvel repositories — so
a free trial never lapses silently and an auto-renewal never charges us by surprise.

It was created in response to the **RecurseML 14-day trial** (started 2026-06-13,
expires 2026-06-27): a trial like that converts to a ~$250/year plan unless a
human decides to keep or cancel it before the clock runs out. This job makes that
clock visible and actionable.

## How it works

```text
data/subscriptions.yml            ← single source of truth (you edit this)
        │
        ▼
scripts/subscription-tracker.js   ← pure verdict engine (trial-expiry / renewal)
        │
        ▼
.github/workflows/                ← daily sweep, upserts ONE tracking issue
  subscription-tracker.yml
```

- **`data/subscriptions.yml`** — the inventory. Each entry records the vendor,
  status (`trial` / `active` / `cancelled`), trial/renewal dates, cost, the
  repositories it applies to, and where to manage it. See the field reference at
  the top of that file.
- **`scripts/subscription-tracker.js`** — computes, per subscription, the
  *effective due date* (a trial's `trial_end` while on trial, otherwise
  `renewal_date`) and a verdict: `ok`, `due_soon`, `expired`, `unknown`, or
  `cancelled`. All logic is pure and clock-injectable, and is unit-tested in
  `tests/subscription-tracker.test.js`.
- **`.github/workflows/subscription-tracker.yml`** — runs daily (13:00 UTC) and
  on demand. It renders the report and **upserts a single issue** titled
  `📅 Subscription & Trial Tracker` (label: `subscriptions`), editing the same
  issue in place so trackers never pile up. Anything expiring or renewing inside
  the warning window (default **7 days**) is listed under **Action needed**.

## Run it locally

```bash
# Print the current report (Markdown, same body the issue gets)
node scripts/subscription-tracker.js

# Use a custom warning window
node scripts/subscription-tracker.js --warn-within-days=14

# Exit non-zero if anything is e
```

=== scripts/sync-bom.sh (head) ===
#!/bin/bash
# Sync BOM — Regenerates docs/_MASTER_BOM.md from individual project BOM files
# Usage: ./scripts/sync-bom.sh
# Run from the revvel-standards repo root

set -euo pipefail

DOCS_DIR="$(dirname "$0")/../docs"
MASTER_BOM="$DOCS_DIR/_MASTER_BOM.md"
TODAY=$(date +"%Y-%m-%d")

echo "======================================"
echo "  Revvel BOM Sync"
echo "======================================"
echo ""

# Find all project BOM files
BOM_FILES=()
while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
  BOM_FILES+=("$f")
done < <(find "$DOCS_DIR" -name "BOM.md" -not -path "$DOCS_DIR/BOM.md" -print0 | sort -z)

if [ ${#BOM_FILES[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "No BOM.md files found in $DOCS_DIR"
  exit 1
```

## Growth and Adoption Trends

Ollama has accumulated over 169,000 stars on GitHub and continues to accelerate its growth trajectory through 2026. The platform's rapid adoption reflects a broader shift in the AI industry: privacy, data sovereignty, and local control have become primary concerns for organizations deploying artificial intelligence at scale.

## Enterprise Use Cases

Enterprise adoption is driven by air-gapped production in defense, finance, healthcare; GDPR-compliant processing without third-party data transfers; edge deployment; cost optimization by eliminating per-token API costs for high-volume workloads; and sub-100ms first-token latency on local hardware. The financial services industry represents one of the earliest and most active adoption domains, with investment firms requiring rapid analysis of confidential documents, legal contracts, and market research without exposing strategic information to third-party services.

## Model Availability

Ollama supports over 100 models from every major open-source provider: Meta's Llama 3.3, Mistral's Nemo and Large, Google's Gemma 2 and 3, Microsoft's Phi-4, Alibaba's Qwen 2.5 series, and DeepSeek's V3 and R1.

## Cloud APIs Still Have a Role

However, the sources indicate this isn't a complete replacement scenario. Cloud APIs remain the better choice when frontier model quality is non-negotiable, as GPT-4o and Claude 3.5 Sonnet still outperform every open-weight model on complex reasoning tasks by 5-15% on standard benchmarks.

1:name: Stuck WR Detector & Auto-Healer
2:on:
---
name: Stuck WR Detector & Auto-Healer
on:
  # ── PREVIOUS APPROACH (kept for the record, intentionally not removed) ──────
  # Originally this healer relied ONLY on the cron sweep below. That routine was
  # added back when OpenRouter was live and many agents worked in PARALLEL on
  # the same WRs at once — label churn and racing runs meant a WR could get its
  # PR-creation run cancelled/skipped, so a periodic sweep was the safety net
  # that caught those errors. It worked, but it leaned on two fragile things:
  #   1. label *timing* — a WR is only "ready" once research:complete lands, and
  #      the event that set it could race the sweep; and
  #   2. GitHub's schedule — which is throttled under load (observed ~50–70 min
  #      between */30 runs), so a just-completed WR could sit ~1h with no PR
  #      (this is exactly what stranded WR #14545).
  #
  # ── NEW APPROACH (why it's better) ─────────────────────────────────────────
  # We still keep the cron as a backstop, but we no longer DEPEND on it for
  # timeliness, and we no longer depend on label-churn events for timing. The
  # `workflow_run` trigger fires the sweep the moment research actually
  # completes, so a ready WR with no PR is healed within minutes regardless of
  # how badly GitHub is throttling cron. Labels (research:complete/wr:complete)
  # are still used — but only as a *completion signal* (a state marker), never
  # as the timing mechanism. That's the "don't rely on labels" point: relying on
  # a label to EXIST is fine; relying on label-event timing + a throttled cron
  # is what burned us.
  # Auto-triggers (schedule cron + workflow_run) are intentionally disabled:
  # the */30 sweep and Research-Engine-completion retriggers caused retrigger
  # storms that escalated stuck WRs into [AUTO-ERROR] issues (e.g. #14592,
  # #14599). The detector is now manual-only — run it deliberately when needed.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:

Upserts a SINGLE tracking issue (label:\n# auditor-controller) so the repo never accumulates duplicate audit issues.\n#\n# Add new assertions by editing scripts/auditor-controller.js \u2192 CHECKS.\n\non:\n  schedule:\n    - '.github/workflows/secrets-sentinel.yml'\n      - 'data/subscriptions.yml'\n\npermissions:\n  contents: read\n  issues: write\n\nconcurrency:\n  group: auditor-controller\n  cancel-in-progress: false\n\njobs:\n  audit:\n    name: Run recurring-failure audit\n    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4.2.2\n\n      - name: Generate report\n        id: audit\n        run: |\n          set +e\n          node scripts/auditor-controller.js > /tmp/audit-report.md\n          rc=$?\n          echo \"exit_code=$rc\" >> \"$GITHUB_OUTPUT\"\n          cat /tmp/audit-report.md >> \"$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY\"\n          # Also run with --check so exit_code reflects failures\n          node scripts/auditor-controller.js --check\n          echo \"check_exit=$?\" >> \"$GITHUB_OUTPUT\"\n          exit 0\n\n      - name: Upsert single tracking issue\n        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'\n        uses: actions/github-script@v9.0.0\n        with:\n          script: |\n            const fs = require('fs');\n            const body = fs.readFileSync('/tmp/audit-report.md', 'utf8');\n            const marker = '<!-- auditor-controller -->';\n            const title = '\ud83d\udee1\ufe0f Auditor Controller \u2014 recurring-failure audit';\n\n            const { data: open } = await github.rest.issues.listForRepo({\n              owner: context.repo.owner, repo: context.repo.repo,\n              state: 'open', per_page: 100,\n            });\n            const existing = open.find(i => !i.pull_request && i.title === title);\n\n            if (existing) {\n              await github.rest.issues.update({\n                owner: context.repo.owner, repo: context.repo.repo,\n                issue_number: existing.number, body,\n              });\n              core.info(`Updated #${existing.number}`);\n            } else {\n              try {\n                await github.rest.issues.createLabel({\n                  owner: context.repo.owner, repo: context.repo.repo,\n                  name: 'auditor-controller', color: '6f42c1',\n                  description: 'Recurring-failure audit issue (upserted, single instance)',\n                });\n              } catch (_) { /* label exists */ }\n              const created = await github.rest.issues.create({\n                owner: context.repo.owner, repo: context.repo.repo,\n                title, body, labels: ['auditor-controller'],\n              });\n              core.info(`Created #${created.data.number}`);\n            }\n\n      -
