The repo already has 18+ audit workflows but no meta-controller that **asserts the recurring fixes stay fixed and gates merges when they regress**.\n\nThis PR adds that piece + lands the Doppler kill switch the WRs requested.\n\n## What\n\n### Doppler kill switch (the 5-WR ask)\n\n| File | Change |\n|------|--------|\n| `.github/workflows/secret-persistence-guard.yml` | Doppler API block wrapped in `if false; then # was: if [ -n \"$DOPPLER_TOKEN\" ]` \u2014 one-line revert if ever needed. Cron is already paused (#14436), this stops `workflow_dispatch` from triggering the overwrite too. |\n| `.github/workflows/secrets-sentinel.yml` | Heal step (which calls `gatekeeper-sync.sh` \u2192 Doppler) short-circuits with an explicit `::notice::` and writes empty-result JSON. The tracker issue still shows what's missing; only the auto-write to GitHub Secrets is gated. |\n\n### `scripts/auditor-controller.js` \u2014 one file, 5 assertions\n\n```\ndoppler-disabled       Regression check on the kill switches above\nwr-pr-link             Lists wr/issues/*.md with no linked PR (groundhog day)\nno-root-junk           Throwaway dev files at repo root\nsubscription-dates     data/subscriptions.yml entries missing renewal/trial dates\ndoppler-spread         New Doppler call sites added outside the allowlist\n```\n\nAdding the next assertion is one function in `CHECKS`. Whole controller is one file \u2014 no separate plumbing per check.\n\n### `.github/workflows/auditor-controller.yml`\n\n- Daily 13:00 UTC schedule + `workflow_dispatch`\n- Also fires on PRs that touch any of: the controller, the kill-switched workflows, `data/subscriptions.yml`\n- **Upserts ONE issue** titled `\ud83d\udee1\ufe0f Auditor Controller \u2014 recurring-failure audit` (label: `auditor-controller`) \u2014 never accumulates dupes\n- **On PR: fails CI** if any assertion is red \u2014 the audit gates merges\n\n## Verified locally\n\n```\n$ node scripts/auditor-controller.js --check; echo \"exit: $?\"\n\u2705 Doppler auto-recover is disabled in secret workflows\n\u274c WR-without-PR: 90+ WRs\n\u274c Subscription dates: 7 entries missing\n\u274c Doppler spread: 3 unexpected call sites (added to allowlist in this commit)\nexit: 1\n```\n\n## Notes\n\n- WR-without-PR finding will surface the 90+ groundhog-day backlog in the daily tracking issue \u2014 one place to triage, not 90 separate notifications.\n- Subscription-dates check will keep nagging until the renewal dates for Cursor, Octopus, cubic, CodeRabbit, Bito, Doppler, GitHub Copilot are filled in.\n- Reverting Doppler is one line per file (uncomment the `if false`).\n",

PR: midnghtsapphire/revvel-standards#14679
Author: Copilot
Comment: <untrusted_external_data source="pr_comment">## Pull request overview

Adds a new “auditor controller” lane to prevent recurring automation regressions (notably Doppler-based secret overwrites) and to centralize recurring-failure audits into a single upserted tracking issue, while also landing Doppler kill switches in the two noisy secret workflows.

**Changes:**
- Introduces `scripts/auditor-controller.js` with multiple working-tree assertions (Doppler disabled, WRs without PRs, root junk, subscription date completeness, Doppler callsite allowlist).
- Adds `.github/workflows/auditor-controller.yml` to run the audit on a schedule / dispatch / targeted PR changes, upsert one tracking issue, and gate PRs on failures.
- Disables Doppler auto-heal/auto-recover behavior in `secrets-sentinel.yml` and `secret-persistence-guard.yml`.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 4 out of 4 changed files in this pull request and generated 3 comments.

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| `scripts/auditor-controller.js` | New meta-audit script that generates a markdown report and supports CI gating via `--check`. |
| `.github/workflows/auditor-controller.yml` | New workflow to run the auditor, upsert a single tracking issue, and fail PRs when checks are red. |
| `.github/workflows/secrets-sentinel.yml` | Short-circuits the heal step to prevent Doppler-driven secret writes while keeping tracking issue output. |
| `.github/workflows/secret-persistence-guard.yml` | Wraps Doppler recovery block in an `if false` kill switch to prevent overwriting secrets. |

=== docs/MANUS_DEVELOPMENT_PIPELINE.md (head) ===
# Manus Development Pipeline: From Prompt to Production

This document outlines the standard operating procedure (SOP) for how Manus AI processes user requests, writes code, tests, and deploys to the live DigitalOcean droplet for the GrowlingEyes project.

## 1. Request Intake & Planning (The "Think" Phase)
When a user prompt is received:
1. **Context Analysis**: Manus reviews the prompt against the current project state, recent commits, and the `revvel-standards` specification.
2. **Task Planning**: A multi-phase plan is generated using the `plan` tool. This breaks the request down into logical steps (e.g., Diagnosis → Code Modification → Local Testing → Deployment → Verification).
3. **Communication**: Manus sends an `info` message to acknowledge the request and outline the approach.

## 2. Investigation & Diagnosis (The "See" Phase)
Before writing code, Manus investigates the current state of the application:
1. **File Inspection**: Uses `file` (`read`, `match`) and `shell` (`grep`, `find`) tools to locate relevant components, APIs, and database schemas.
2. **Log Analysis**: If an error is reported, Manus checks PM2 logs (`pm2 logs growlingeyes`) or Nginx error logs on the droplet via SSH.
3. **Live Testing**: Uses `curl` or browser tools to test endpoints and verify the issue in the live environment.

## 3. Code Modification (The "Write" Phase)
Once the issue is understood, Manus modifies the codebase:
1. **Targeted Edits**: Uses the `file` tool (`edit`, `write`) to make precise changes to TypeScript, React components, or configuration files.
2. **Standard Compliance**: Ensures all changes adhere to the `revvel-standards` (e.g., using `fetchWithFallback`, stripping HTML, truncating URLs).
3. **Local Verification**: Runs `npm run build` or `npx tsc --noEmit` in the sandbox to catch syntax or type errors before deployment.

## 4. Deployment & Verification (The "Ship" Phase)
The deployment process is fully automated via SSH:
1. **Build**: Compiles the frontend (Vite) and backend (esbuild) in the sandbox (`npm run build`).
2. **Transfer**: Uses `scp` and `rsync` to push the compiled assets (`dist/index.js` and `dist/public/`) to the DigitalOcean droplet (`164.90.148.7`).
3. **Permissions**: Sets correct ownership and permissions (`chmod -R o+rX /var/www/growlingeyes/dist/public/`) to ensure Nginx can serve the files.
4. **Restart**: Restarts the PM2 process (`pm2 restart growlingeyes --update-env`) to apply backend changes.
5. **Live Check**: Uses `curl` with a browser User-Agent to verify the live site returns HTTP 200 and serves the new assets.

  "content": "# Agent Scaffolding Ban\n\nGenerated AI tools (Lovable, Replit, Manus, Bolt, v0, Cursor, Copilot, Devin,\nGitHub Copilot Workspace, Claude Code, etc.) routinely leave their fingerprints\nin the code they produce: watermark footers, attribution strings, generic Vite\ntest scaffolding the user never asked for, default placeholder pages, generated\nREADME sections, \"Made with X\" badges.\n\nThese are not acceptable in a sellable product. This standard lists the banned\nartifacts and is enforced by `.github/workflows/agent-fingerprint-gate.yml` via\n`scripts/agent-fingerprint-scan.js`.\n\n## What gets blocked\n\n### A. Attribution / \"Made with\" footers\n\nThese strings, anywhere in any file the PR touches, fail the gate:\n\n- `Made with Lovable`, `Built on Lovable`, `Powered by Lovable`\n- `Made with Replit`, `Built on Replit`, `Powered by Replit`\n- `Made with Manus`, `Powered by Manus`\n- `Made with Bolt`, `Powered by Bolt`, `bolt.new` (in user-facing copy)\n- `Made with v0`, `Built with v0`, `v0.dev/` (in user-facing copy)\n- `Generated by Claude`, `Generated by GPT`, `Generated by Cursor`\n- `Co-Authored-By: Claude` in **user-facing files** (allowed in git history)\n\n### B. Default scaffolding pages\n\nThe Vite/CRA/Next.js default app templates **must be replaced** before merge:\n\n- `Welcome to Vite + React` / `Vite + React` / `Vite logo` (default `App.tsx`)\n- `npm run dev` welcome text in any deployed page\n- `getting-started.mdx` / `README-default.md` from a starter\n- The `vite.svg` / `react.svg` default favicons (must be replaced with the product's actual logo)\n- `count is 0` + `setCount((count) => count + 1)` counter (the CRA/Vite default)\n\n### C. Unused test scaffolding\n\nGenerated test files that don't test the actual product, just the template:\n\n- `src/App.test.tsx` that only checks \"renders learn react link\" or \"renders Vite + React\"\n- `src/setupTests.ts` if no test in the repo actually uses it\n- `__tests__/example.spec.ts` (generic placeholder names)\n- `playwright/e2e/example.spec.ts`\n\n### D. Unrequested README sections\n\nWhen the user didn't ask for a README, the agent shouldn't generate boilerplate\nlike:\n\n- \"This project was bootstrapped with Create React App\"\n- \"## Available Scripts\"\n- \"## Learn More\" with links to Vite/React docs\n- \"## Deploy on Vercel\" with the Vercel badge\n\nIf the user wants a README they'll ask. Generic generated ones get blocked.\n\n### E. Watermarked assets\n\nImage / SVG / font assets that contain the generator's name in metadata or\nvisible text:\n\n- SVGs with `<!-- Generated by Manus -->` / `<!-- Created with Lovable -->`\n- PNGs / JPEGs with EXIF `Software: ...` matching banned generators\n- `logo.png` that's actually the Lovable/Replit/Bolt logo\n\n## Allowed\n\nAttribution **inside developer-facing docs** (this `standards/` directory,\n`CONTRIBUTING.md`, etc.) is fine \u2014 credit where due. The rule is about what\nships to users in product code.\n\nGit commit messages may include `Co-Authored-By:` lines per the project's\nexisting convention.\n\n## Exceptions\n\nIf a fingerprint is intentional (e.g., a tutorial product about how to build\nwith Lovable), add `agent-fingerprint:allow <reason>` to the PR body to suppress\nthe gate for that PR only.\n\n## Per-tool profiles\n\nSee `docs/agents/<tool>/PROFILE.md` for tool-specific known fingerprints and\ngotchas as we observe them in practice.\n\n## Re-generating the rule list\n\nAdd new banned strings to `scripts/agent-fingerprint-scan.js` \u2192 `BANNED`.\nThe scanner is the source of truth; this doc explains the why.\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/home/user/revvel-standards/.github/workflows/agent-fingerprint-gate.yml",
  "content": "name: Agent Fingerprint Gate\n# Blocks PRs that ship agent watermarks, default starter scaffolding, unsolicited\n# README boilerplate, or CRA/Vite test placeholders. Standard:\n# standards/AGENT_SCAFFOLDING_BAN.md.\n#\n# Escape hatch: include `agent-fingerprint:allow <reason>` in the PR body.\n\non:\n  pull_request:\n    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, edited]\n\npermissions:\n  contents: read\n\nconcurrency:\n  group: agent-fingerprint-gate-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}\n  cancel-in-progress: true\n\njobs:\n  scan:\n    name: Scan changed files for agent fingerprints\n    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4.2.2\n        with: { fetch-depth: 0 }\n\n      - name: Check PR body for escape hatch\n        id: escape\n        env:\n          PR_BODY: ${{ github.event.pull_request.body }}\n        run: |\n          if printf '%s' \"$PR_BODY\" | grep -qiE 'agent-fingerprint:allow'; then\n            echo \"skip=true\" >> \"$GITHUB_OUTPUT\"\n            echo \"::notice::PR body contains agent-fingerprint:allow \u2014 gate skipped.\"\n          else\n            echo \"skip=false\" >> \"$GITHUB_OUTPUT\"\n          fi\n\n      - name: Run fingerprint scanner on changed files\n        if: steps.escape.outputs.skip != 'true'\n        env:\n          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}\n          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}\n        run: |\n          git diff --name-only --diff-filter=AMR \"${BASE_SHA}...${HEAD_SHA}\" \\\n            | node scripts/agent-fingerprint-scan.js --changed\n"
}

  "content": "# Claude \u2014 Profile\n\nHow Claude (Claude Code, web app, API) processes input so you can adapt your\nprompts. Living doc \u2014 update as you observe more.\n\n## Models you'd actually use\n\n- **Opus 4.7 / 4.8** \u2014 heavy code, multi-step reasoning, audit work. Expensive\n  per token.\n- **Sonnet 4.6** \u2014 most agent surfaces wrap this; balanced.\n- **Haiku 4.5** \u2014 cheap classifications, label sorts, light queries.\n- **Fable 5** \u2014 fast / streaming preview lane.\n\n## How it processes\n\n- Extended-thinking trace is where the real reasoning lives. The UI hides it\n  after the response posts. The JSONL transcript (`/root/.claude/projects/...`)\n  keeps it. Capture this \u2014 it's the most useful data for tuning prompts.\n- Defaults to asking clarifying questions when a request is even slightly\n  ambiguous. Burns tokens. Counter with: \"no questions, do the smallest\n  defensible version.\"\n- Defaults to \"let me explain the architecture first\" before doing. Counter with:\n  \"no architecture pitch \u2014 just produce the file.\"\n- Tends to recap your message back at you before responding. Counter with:\n  \"don't echo me; respond only.\"\n- Defaults to multi-phase plans. Counter with: \"one iteration, full version.\"\n\n## What it's actually good at\n\n- Bash, YAML, regex edge cases (heredoc escaping, shell injection, command\n  substitution).\n- Cross-file refactors that follow an existing contract.\n- Diagnosing audit-style problems across many workflows.\n- Writing markdown that doesn't read as AI-generated.\n\n## What it tends to over-engineer\n\n- Architecture pitches when you wanted output.\n- Phase 1/2/3 plans when you wanted the whole thing.\n- \"Want me to ...?\" follow-up questions instead of acting.\n- Verbose commit messages.\n- Adding emojis when you didn't ask.\n\n## What it tends to hallucinate\n\n- Files it didn't create (cites paths that don't exist).\n- Tool flags/options (especially less-common CLI tools).\n- API endpoints (defaults to plausible-looking URLs that 404).\n- Sometimes claims a commit SHA exists when it's about to be produced\n  (related: marks something \"\u2705 Resolved\" referring to in-flight work that\n  hasn't pushed yet).\n\n## Token-economy gotchas\n\n- Each \"?\" you write earns a long preamble before any work. Statements get\n  faster, shorter responses than questions.\n- Mid-task webhook noise (Vercel build comments, Ship Quality PASS, etc.)\n  earns acknowledgment turns. Use slash-command rules to mute classes of these.\n- Worktree/sandbox subagents multiply cost \u2014 only spawn when work is genuinely\n  parallel.\n\n## What works as prompt shape\n\n- \"Do X. No questions. Stop talking when done.\" \u2014 terse, action-only.\n- \"Receive only, no solving\" (brain-dump mode) followed by \"sort\" \u2014 separates\n  capture from triage.\n- Concrete file paths + line numbers in the prompt \u2014 drops research overhead.\n- \"Use existing pattern: <path>\" \u2014 prevents re-design.\n\n## Fingerprints to watch (enforced by `agent-fingerprint-scan.js`)\n\n- `Generated by Claude` in user-facing files (allowed in dev docs only).\n- `Co-Authored-By: Claude` in user-facing files (allowed in git commit messages).\n- Emoji-heavy README sections unless explicitly asked.\n\n## Session capture\n\n`.claude/hooks/save-transcript.sh` lifts the raw JSONL to\n`docs/agents/claude/transcripts/<date>-<topic>.md` on session end so the\nthinking blocks survive.\n"
}

Falls back to the newest JSONL in the project\n# transcript dir if the env var is missing.\n\nset -euo pipefail\n\nREPO_ROOT=\"$(cd \"$(dirname \"$0\")/../..\" && pwd)\"\nOUT_DIR=\"$REPO_ROOT/docs/agents/claude/transcripts\"\nmkdir -p \"$OUT_DIR\"\n\n# Locate transcript: prefer the env var Claude Code provides; otherwise pick\n# the newest JSONL under ~/.claude/projects matching this repo.\nSRC=\"\"\nif [[ -n \"${CLAUDE_TRANSCRIPT_PATH:-}\" && -f \"$CLAUDE_TRANSCRIPT_PATH\" ]]; then\n  SRC=\"$CLAUDE_TRANSCRIPT_PATH\"\nelse\n  PROJECT_DIR=$(echo \"$REPO_ROOT\" | tr '/' '-' | sed 's/^-//')\n  CANDIDATE_DIR=\"$HOME/.claude/projects/-$PROJECT_DIR\"\n  if [[ -d \"$CANDIDATE_DIR\" ]]; then\n    SRC=$(ls -1t \"$CANDIDATE_DIR\"/*.jsonl 2>/dev/null | head -1 || true)\n  fi\nfi\n\nif [[ -z \"$SRC\" || ! -f \"$SRC\" ]]; then\n  echo \"save-transcript: no transcript found; skipping.\" >&2\n  exit 0\nfi\n\nDATE=\"$(date -u '+%Y-%m-%d-%H%M%S')\"\nSESSION_ID=\"$(basename \"$SRC\" .jsonl)\"\nRAW_OUT=\"$OUT_DIR/${DATE}-${SESSION_ID}.jsonl\"\nMD_OUT=\"$OUT_DIR/${DATE}-${SESSION_ID}.md\"\n\n# Always keep the raw \u2014 that's the source of truth.\ncp -f \"$SRC\" \"$RAW_OUT\"\n\n# Render a readable Markdown version.
